title: Removable dentures
what: A denture replaces several or all of your teeth. You take it out and put it back in yourself to clean it.
why: When many or all teeth are missing, and fixed options are not suitable.
duration: usually 3 to 5 visits over a few weeks; getting used to it usually takes a few weeks to a couple of months
tell_doctor: Gum problems, sores, or a dry mouth
If you wore dentures before, and what did not suit you

prepare.title: Treatment
prepare.text: Any remaining teeth and the gums are treated first. Sometimes some teeth are removed.

prepare.title: Old denture
prepare.text: If you have an old denture, bring it.

bring: Your old denture, if you have one
Dental X-rays, if you have them
steps: The dentist examines your mouth and discusses the type of denture
Your bite is recorded, and the color and shape of the teeth are chosen
A wax model is tried in
The finished denture is fitted and adjusted
After a few days, sore spots are adjusted
feel: At first, the denture feels big, and you may have more saliva
Your speech may change for a few days
Sore spots may appear. They are fixed at the adjustment visit
after: Start with soft food cut into small pieces
Read aloud to get used to speaking faster
Clean the denture every day. At night, do as your dentist says
Do not bend or adjust the denture yourself
red_flags: A sore in your mouth that does not heal in 1 to 2 weeks: see your dentist

faq.q: Can I sleep with my denture in?
faq.a: Usually you are advised to take it out at night so your gums can rest. Ask your dentist.

faq.q: How long does it take to get used to it?
faq.a: Usually a few weeks. Wear the denture every day. This helps you get used to it faster.

reminders.text: Denture visit tomorrow. Bring your old denture, if you have one.
